In Blazor we use the .NET trimmer to significantly reduce the publish size of Blazor WebAssembly apps. However, we don\\u0026#39;t currently use the .NET trimmer to its fullest potential. We currently configure the trimmer in a partial mode, which only trims assemblies that are explicitly marked as trimmable. This typically means that the app assembly itself and many dependencies are not trimmed. This is a conservative setting that optimizes for maintaining functionality over reducing app size. \\n\\nThe default trim mode for the .NET trimmer is to trim everything. This is the mode used by the .NET Native AOT workloads.Analyzers provide warnings if there are code paths in the app that are not safe to trim. Given how sensitive web apps are to download size and load time, it seems like doing full trimming should be the goal for Blazor.\\n\\nEnabling support for full trimming also is a potential solution to enabling a [single project model for Blazor Web Apps](#49079) that target both server and browser. When you multitarget a project, everything in the project is built for both targets unless you indicated otherwise. This is problematic for browser scenarios because you may potentially bring in dependencies, components, and code into the browser targeted build that are only needed on the server. However, if we could enable full trimming *and* indicate to the trimmer which components are setup to render on WebAssembly, then the browser build could be aggressively trimmed to remove any unwanted code and dependencies.\\n\\nEnabling support for full .NET trimming typically means removing any dynamic code path that are based on reflection. We would need to make Blazor apps trimmer friendly by removing this code using techniques like source generators. For example, in Blazor we use reflection as part of the component discovery process and in the render tree builder code generated by the Razor compiler. We\\u0026#39;re already working on enabling [component discovery through source generation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/48767). We also have on our backlog to [handle component parameters through source generation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/29550). There may be other related work items as well.\\n\\nThere is also ecosystem impact of enabling full trimming by default. Many .NET libraries are not setup for trimming and would potentially need to be updated. It will take some time to work through these issues with the Blazor community. Certain features also simply wouldn\\u0026#39;t work with full trimming. For example, dynamically loading dependencies at runtime that are not known statically. For backwards compatibility, app developers can configure the trimmer to not trim assemblies that are not yet trimmer friendly. We\\u0026#39;d need to understand better all the cases that get impacted by full trimming and ensure we provide a reasonable user experience for addressing them.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/49409\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"danroth27\",\"id\":1874516,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/danroth27\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1874516?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"Priority:1\",\"Pillar: Technical Debt\",\"feature-trimming\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":20,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":46,\"+1\":43,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":3},\"created_at\":\"2023-07-14T14:49:12Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-12-06T11:52:00Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

It has a few pages rendered on the server (SSR) and a \\u0026#34;counter\\u0026#34; page configured as:\\n`@rendermode InteractiveAuto`\\nI don\\u0026#39;t know if it is important but server doesn\\u0026#39;t support web sockets - Blazor fallbacks to polling in server interactive mode.\\n\\nOld version worked correctly in Firefox with javascript.options.wasm disabled. WASM files were not loaded and the application was running in server interactive mode. Then I enabled the javascript.options.wasm  option and refreshed the page. The WASM files were loaded and the application worked in client interactive mode.\\n\\nCurrently (in .NET 8.0.2) \\u0026#34;counter\\u0026#34; page is prerendered on the server and displayed in the browser but browser displays this message in console:\\nUncaught (in promise) Error: This browser does not support WebAssembly.\\n\\nIn my opinion for pages (or whole application) configured to work as `InteractiveAuto` you should use server interactive mode if WASM is not available.\\n\\nYou can go even further. Let\\u0026#39;s assume my WASM application is published with support for SIMD instructions (this is default configuration in 8.0). Unfortunately they are not available in iOS 15.x. You should test for SIMD support and fallback to SSI mode in case it is not supported. Related issue: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/48756\\n\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n_No response_\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/54233\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"Andrzej-W\",\"id\":32604409,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/Andrzej-W\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/32604409?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":6,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":1,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2024-02-26T20:52:36Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-02-18T15:25:30Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

(No-nos like passing lambdas as parameters)\\n- One Child Component for some reason is rerendered 10 times on changes.\\n- Some component maybe throws unintended events which caues rerenders.\\n- A costly operation (Rest call) is executed while wating for the task to complete multiple renders happen.\\n- A REST Call is made in OnParametersSet() or OnAfterRender() and by error this rest call is executed multiple times since unexpected Rerenders.\\n\\nWith one Component this can be debugged with console messages in OnParametersSet() or OnAfterRender, but in case of a complex render three with different components this gets quite compilcated to diagnose Performance Bottlenecks.\\n\\nAlso it is often difficult to see which changes cause rerenders in child components. \\nOr which await calls for for responses from Webservices also cause rerenders between initiating the call and completing the call.\\n\\n## Potential Solution:\\n\\nSome possiblily / Component / API, which allows globally to trace all OnSetParameters, Renders etc. with execution times, to see\\nif renders happen too frequent, how long it is executed and what caues the bottlenecks.\\n\\nat first maybe an API to hook into the render events of all components would be maybe already enough. Otherwise I would need make a custom ComponentBase class which traces all Steps like BuildRenderTree() or OnAfterRender().\\n\\n## Example\\n\\nA example output log\\n\\n```\\nNavigation.Component1 InitalizeAsync() took 100 Milliseconds\\nNavigation.Component1 Inital Render:\\nNavigation.Component1 BuildRenderTree() took 10 milliseconds\\nNavigation.Component1.SubComponent Initalize() took 400 milliseconds\\nNavigation.Component1 Inital Render:\\nNavigation.Component1 Render because parameter change.\\nNavigation.Component1.SubComponent BuildRenderTree() took 10 milliseconds\\nNavigation.Component1 Render because parameter change.\\nNavigation.Component1.SubComponent BuildRenderTree() took 10 milliseconds\\nNavigation.Component1 Render because parameter change.\\nNavigation.Component1.SubComponent BuildRenderTree() took 10 milliseconds\\nNavigation.Component1 Render because eventhanlder onclick\\nNavigation.Component1.SubComponent BuildRenderTree() took 10 milliseconds\\n```\\n\\nA integration into the Performance Monitor is maybe possible in Blazor Server Side but on the Blazor Webassembly side\\nonly general Browser tools for Webassembly would be possible. To improve performance on certain pages, I’ve added static SSR-enabled pages using the `ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting attribute`.\\nTo enhance the user experience, I created an empty component called `WasmStarter` in the client project. In `App.razor`, when the global render mode of `` and `` is null because `HttpContext.AcceptsInteractiveRouting()` is `false`, I included `WasmStarter` with Blazor WASM render mode. This allows Blazor WASM to download and start in the background while users interact with the static SSR-enabled page content! ❤️\\n\\nThis approach works, but with these two issues:\\n\\n1- When navigating from a static SSR-enabled page to a Blazor WASM page, Blazor sends an unnecessary XHR request to fetch that page(!). Install the .NET 11 Preview 5 SDK (`11.0.100-preview.5.26272.118`).\\n2. `dotnet new blazorwasm -o WasmTest`\\n3. `cd WasmTest`\\n4. `dotnet run`\\n5. Open `http://localhost:/` in a browser.\\n6. Request path: \\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;{**fallback:nonfile}\\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;. Physical path: \\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;...\\\\obj\\\\Debug\\\\net11.0\\\\compressed\\\\...gz\\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;\\ninfo: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.EndpointMiddleware[1]\\n      Executed endpoint \\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.RouteEndpoint\\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;\\ninfo: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics[2]\\n      Request finished HTTP/1.1 GET http://localhost:5000/ - 200 1376 text/html 302.9165ms\\n```\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\nNone.\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n11.0.100-preview.5.26272.118\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n- OS: Windows 11\\n- Template: `dotnet new blazorwasm` (standalone)\\n- Reproduces with `dotnet run`, `dotnet watch`, and Visual Studio Insiders F5\\n- Same template on .NET 10 (`net10.0`) is significantly quieter\\n\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/66879\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"danroth27\",\"id\":1874516,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/danroth27\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1874516?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"Regression\"],\"assignees\":[\"javiercn\"],\"milestone\":\"11.0-preview7\",\"comments\":2,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-05-28T07:11:30Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-07-22T17:50:22Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2026-07-22T17:50:22Z\",\"closed_by\":\"danroth27\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":1,\"references\":[{\"number\":67048,\"title\":\"Align gateway and templates with Aspire implementation\",\"state\":\"MERGED\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67048\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"}]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Full reloads (`forceLoad: true`) or `@rendermode InteractiveServer` preserve state correctly.\\n\\n### To Reproduce\\n```bash\\ngit clone https://github.com/CoCoNuTeK/-PersistentState-AllowUpdates-true-issue-when-InteractiveWebAssembly.git\\ncd -PersistentState-AllowUpdates-true-issue-when-InteractiveWebAssembly/PersistenceStateIssue\\ndotnet run\\n```\\n\\n1. Open `http://localhost:5041/persist-demo-b` in Chrome with DevTools open.\\n2. Observe initial console output, for example:\\n   ```\\n   [PersistDemoB] Skipping random value generation because state already contains \\u0026#39;39\\u0026#39;.\\n   [PersistDemoA] No persisted random value found. Simulating load before generating a new value.\\n   [PersistDemoA] Generated random value \\u0026#39;72\\u0026#39;.\\n   [PersistDemoB] No persisted random value found. Simulating load before generating a new value.\\n   [PersistDemoB] Generated random value \\u0026#39;25\\u0026#39;.\\n   ```\\n3. Use the on-page buttons (which call `NavigateTo(..., forceLoad: false)`) to switch between `/persist-demo-a` and `/persist-demo-b`.\\n4. Each enhanced navigation triggers another execution of `OnInitializedAsync` in the WASM instance and generates a new random value, despite the Network tab showing the prerender and `[PersistentState(AllowUpdates = true)]` being present.\\n5. For example:\\n\\n50 / 50 = 100%\\n50 / 51 = 98%\\n\\nThis results in the visible progress changing from 100% back to 98%, which\\nlooks broken and unprofessional to users.\\n\\nExpected behavior:\\n\\n- The total number of startup resources should be fixed before progress is reported.\\n- Progress must never decrease.\\n- 100% must only be reported after all required startup resources are loaded.\\n- Ideally, progress should represent downloaded bytes instead of only a resource count.\\n\\nPlease treat this as a correctness bug in the built-in Blazor loading indicator,\\nnot only as a feature request.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe built-in Blazor WebAssembly loading progress must be monotonic.\\n\\nOnce the progress reaches 100%, it must never decrease again. Create a standard Blazor WebAssembly application.\\n2. Replace the contents of wwwroot/index.html with the code above.\\n3. Publish and serve the application.\\n4. Open the browser developer console.\\n5. Reload the page.\\n\\nThe observer records all changes to Blazor\\u0026#39;s\\n--blazor-load-percentage CSS variable.\\n\\nOn the affected production application, the observed sequence included:\\n\\n87.74% -\\u0026gt; 100% -\\u0026gt; 96.30% -\\u0026gt; 99.38% -\\u0026gt; 100%\\n\\nThe browser console reports \\u0026#34;Progress decreased\\u0026#34; when the value moves\\nbackwards after already reaching 100%.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\nNETCoreApp,Version=v10.0\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n    \\u0026#34;name\\u0026#34;: \\u0026#34;.NETCoreApp,Version=v10.0\\u0026#34;,\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67979\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"RoellinRacing\",\"id\":154523119,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/RoellinRacing\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/154523119?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":1,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-07-23T12:16:30Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T06:27:27Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Please describe the problem.\\n\\nI was very excited to see that with .NET 7 Blazor team has introduced download progress. Bundle size is known limitation of Blazor client, nice and informative progress bar is essential for any serious web app to mitigate this problem. To achieve this essential goal our team has to use custom loader. DIY solutions in such sensitive area are quite dangerous - each error or bug in this area means potentially lost customer. Therefore we were about to drop our custom loader with new .NET but soon realised that blazor progress shows completely bogus data.\\nI don\\u0026#39;t know how Blazor computes total progress but here\\u0026#39;s what we encountered with:\\nTotal AOT bundle size is 137 Mb (which is much, but we can put up with) dotnet.wasm occupying the largest part of that:\\n![Screenshot 2023-02-09 at 11 05 41](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3992180/217791641-819de078-5bcf-4740-a6ed-b2665c869500.png)\\nSo, real download progress is 19%, whereas here\\u0026#39;s what Blazor shows:\\n![Screenshot 2023-02-09 at 11 09 07](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3992180/217792641-b67d5672-25f7-4ef9-bd1e-d1c1f4350fb5.png)\\n\\nIt got stuck at 98% for the rest of 100Mb of download. Such user experience is even worse than indefinite spinner because it misleading that application is frozen and nothing happens at all. At current state I find this feature useless or even harmful.\\n\\n\\n### Describe the solution you\\u0026#39;d like\\n\\nBundle download state should be explicitly exposed. Developers should have access via JS to bundle size, total progress, eventually to a flag that progress is not responding.\\nIdeally all pieces of information related to bundle should be available to developers  for providing the best user experience:\\n\\n- Total bundle size\\n- Current progress\\n- Individual item size\\n- Individual item progress\\n- Download speed\\n- Estimated time\\n\\n### Additional context\\n\\n_No response_\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/46549\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"elepner\",\"id\":3992180,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/elepner\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/3992180?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"feature-blazor-wasm\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":3,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2023-02-09T11:03:07Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2024-10-30T21:21:24Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}
